text.en: A plant has no stove, yet it makes its own food. Its leaves are tiny kitchens that use sunlight. We learn how plants make food, take in water and breathe.

Photosynthesis is how green plants make food. Leaves take in carbon dioxide from air through tiny pores called stomata, and roots take in water. Chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves, captures sunlight. Using the light, the plant turns carbon dioxide and water into glucose and releases oxygen. The glucose is stored as starch. This is why plants are called producers.
Roots take water and minerals from the soil. Xylem tubes carry water upward to the leaves. Phloem tubes carry food from leaves to other parts.
Transpiration is the loss of water as vapour from the leaves through stomata. It cools the plant and pulls water up from the roots.
Plants also respire: they take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide, day and night. Some plants, like insect-eating pitcher plants, get extra nutrients from insects.

problem.en: What does a plant need to make food?

text.en: Sunlight, carbon dioxide, water and chlorophyll.

prompt.en: Explain why plants are important for animals.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking plants breathe only at night.

points.en: Xylem carries water; phloem carries food.
